Subject: Regional control plane handshake + subprocessor schedule

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ApexCloud is excited about Redwood's low-latency serving options. Before we proceed to the pilot, our legal and ops teams need a compact operational plan that covers:

- Which control plane components will be instantiated in-region versus cross-region (control plane vs data plane split)
- A short, timeboxed schedule for subprocessor disclosure (we require an initial roster, then a final roster 21 days before go-live)
- An agreed fallback window and notification SLA if transient cross-region processing is needed (we typically ask for a max 72-hour ephemeral window and 24h notice)

Can you confirm if Redwood can provide: a one-page control-plane diagram, the initial subprocessor roster by EOD Monday, and an ops fallback runbook? I attached a template for the roster to speed things up.

Also: legal flagged key management flow — will customer-managed KMS be available for the pilot, or do we need to rely on Redwood-managed keys?

Appreciate a consolidated reply so I can loop in our CISO.

Best,
Susan Park
Director, Cloud Integrations
ApexCloud

Hi Susan — great to hear and thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I'll follow with the artifacts you asked for.

1) Control plane vs data plane: Redwood supports a split deployment for Private/Dedicated customers. For the pilot we propose: control plane (orchestration, route decisions, metrics ingestion) in the us-west-2 control cluster; data plane (model inference) pinned to the customer-selected region (us-east-1 for your pilot). This avoids cross-region model tokenization while allowing central observability.

2) Subprocessor schedule: we can provide an initial roster tomorrow (2027-05-23) and the final roster no later than 2027-06-01 (well before your 21-day requirement for a planned go-live).

3) Fallback window: we agree to a transient cross-region processing window up to 72 hours for critical failover, with proactive notification. Redwood's standard notice is 24 hours; for ApexCloud we can commit to 24h notice + a short post-event summary within 48h. We'll also include automatic routing policies to minimize cross-border hops.

KMS: for the pilot we can provision a customer-managed KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) that covers at-rest encryption for model cache keys and long-term artifacts. Some ephemeral telemetry still routes through our control plane; we can document the telemetry path in the diagram.

I'll attach a one-page control-plane sketch, the draft DPA addendum Marissa prepared, and the ops fallback runbook. Kimberly/Karthik — can you confirm the telemetry fields that will transit the control plane so Susan can validate with CISO?

Next steps: I will send the initial roster (template filled) by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Head of Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi team — quick technical note for Susan and Apex ops:

Telemetry that will traverse the control plane (us-west-2) is limited to routing metadata and anonymized request metrics. Specifically: request id, timestamp, model id, token count, latency bucket, and error flag. No raw input texts or embeddings are sent to the control plane — those remain in-region in the data plane unless the fallback window is triggered.

When fallback is in effect, we will only replicate the minimum fields needed for inference fallback and will respect your data minimization settings. All telemetry in the control plane will be logged with a 30-day retention by default (we can extend or shorten per contract).

Regarding KMS: the BYOK flow we support uses a customer-managed key in the customer's AWS account; we only store a key reference in our control plane (no key material). All cryptographic operations for stored artifacts use the customer's key via cross-account IAM roles. I can share the AWS ARN pattern you'll need to provision.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
